National remote areas and diplomacy
Clinical care and long-term follow-up
Cultivate clinical materials and provide somatic-cell therapies with long-term follow-up.
Treatment shifts from one-time relief to continuous service.
Should we protect routine consultations first, or allocate culture materials to modification?
Routine care and material cultivation are coordinated by the on-duty team according to stock levels.
Closed-loop water and soil engineering
Condition soil, circulate clean water, and build low-consumption public facilities.
Ordinary residents can also gain stable food supplies and living conditions.
Engineers and construction materials must be diverted at first to reduce fuel expenditure later.
There is no need to request water and soil restoration supplies batch by batch.
Prosthetics and neural interfaces
Fabricate medical prosthetics and assistive exoskeletons; recipients retain their biological bodies.
Return to work without removing food rations or clinical needs.
Should scarce parts be prioritized for assistive limbs, or allocated to the production line?
Prosthetic maintenance is incorporated into routine public maintenance.
Verifiable automation
Restricted machines take on part of the routine work.
Equipment assists people at work; equipment does not count as population.
Repetitive exertion is reduced, but the burdens of power supply and maintenance increase.
Production quotas and shutdown safeguards are overseen by the entrusted team.
Safe somatic-cell editing
Willing residents undergo traceable adaptive somatic-cell modification.
Modified groups can take on heavier environmental restoration work.
Informed consent, treatment priority, and genetic boundaries must be agreed upon first.
There is no need to track follow-up individually; cases enter the routine clinical queue.
Environmental adaptation and ecological monitoring
Under close monitoring, modified groups participate in the restoration of polluted areas.
They can live alongside ordinary residents without changing their civic status.
Routine monitoring and medication must be maintained; a missed check will allow complications to accumulate.
Scattered repeated field surveys are taken over by a permanent ecological institution.
Complete ecological public network
Closed-loop agriculture, public healthcare, and schooling form a complete network for ordinary life.
Operations can continue without changing anyone's body.
Invest in labor and land-based infrastructure in exchange for lower dependence on power and parts.
Daily provision, maintenance, and surplus-food exports are handled automatically according to the reserve floor.
Complete bodies and continuous identity
With the person's consent, the same continuous identity is transferred into a complete mechanical body.
No longer consumes food, but requires continuous power, maintenance, and cooling.
The mechanical body belongs to its owner; existing property, rights, and responsibilities continue with it. Running a second copy at the same time is strictly forbidden.
Routine small-scale parts stocking is coordinated by the maintenance network.
Continuous-identity maintenance network
Provide limited energy storage, power-loss hibernation, and restoration of the same identity.
During a power outage, energy is restricted and hibernation begins first; a backup cannot be registered as a second person.
Reserve parts and emergency power must be set aside specifically and cannot all be diverted to expand production.
